name: dark-forest-mainnet
description: Sponsors Dark Forest gameplay on Aztec mainnet: a per-player daily allowance of free transactions, restricted to the game's player-facing contracts. Admin and Config contracts are deliberately excluded.

policy._comment_maxFeeWei: Measured on 2026-07-29: costliest sponsored path (first-of-day) cost 7595511600000 wei; this is that x3 headroom. Re-calibrate against mainnet before funding, since fee levels differ.

_comment_maxLossWei: $20 at AZTEC ~= $0.0146 => ~1370 fee juice. Funding never exceeds this; the paymaster has no withdraw.
_comment_allowedTargets: Player-facing gameplay contracts only. Addresses may be literals or 'env:VAR_NAME'. Deliberately absent: ADMIN and CONFIG (admin operations must not be sponsored) and all storage contracts (players never call them directly).
_comment_allowedAccountClasses: ONLY the initializerless Schnorr class from @aztec/accounts 5.0.1 — what the embedded wallet actually uses. The plain SchnorrAccount class is deliberately EXCLUDED: it is published on deploy, and a published account can call ContractInstanceRegistry::update to upgrade itself to hostile code, which would be sponsored (the paymaster can only see the ORIGINAL class). Initializerless accounts send no deploy tx, so they are unpublished and cannot upgrade — see requireUnpublishedAccounts. Class ids hash the artifact (version-pinned, network-independent); the deploy script recomputes them from the installed packages and refuses to deploy on a mismatch. Bumping @aztec/accounts changes these ids and requires an FPC redeploy for players on the new version.
_comment_requireUnpublishedAccounts: Keep true. This is what makes the class allowlist bind the code that will actually execute rather than merely the class the account was created with.
